sections.h2: Where the Boca Raton tax bill comes from
sections.html:
A single bill arrives from the Palm Beach County Tax Collector, and the Property Appraiser sets the value. The city itself levies only a slice: the city's August 2026 Property Taxes Explained brochure shows eight taxing authorities on a Boca Raton bill, with 21.67 percent of the tax going to the city.

Bills are mailed by November 1, more than 600,000 of them, to the address the Property Appraiser has on file. Taxes are payable from November 1 through March 31.

  • Value, exemptions and mailing address: Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, (561) 355-2866.
  • Bills, delinquent tax, installment plan, deferral and tax certificates: Palm Beach County Tax Collector, delinquent line (561) 355-2264.
  • City levy and fire assessment: City of Boca Raton, 201 West Palmetto Park Road.

Eight authorities appear: the Palm Beach County School Board, Palm Beach County operating and debt, Boca Raton operating and debt, the Health Care District, the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District, the Children's Services Council, the South Florida Water Management District and the Florida Inland Navigational District.

sections.h2: The city's own rate over time
sections.html:
The city's operating rate sat near 3.45 mills in 2018 and is shown at 3.6476 mills for both 2026 and 2027, while a separate debt service rate fell from 0.2245 to 0.0163 over the same stretch. Combined, the city's total millage moved only between 3.6788 and 3.6639 across the ten years charted. The 2027 column is the city's proposed figure, so read it as a plan, not a final bill.

Because the city's slice has held steady, larger swings in a Boca Raton bill come from the school board and county lines.

Fire protection is billed as a non-ad valorem assessment, printed at $170.00, which sits on the bill beside the millage. Unincorporated Palm Beach County instead pays a fire MSTU based on assessed value.

sections.h2: What the city levy pays for
sections.html:
The city's operating budget is $723,811,900, with 1,951 full time equivalent employees, 224 police officers and 269 firefighters working from 8 fire stations. It handles 47,161 police calls and 18,872 fire and rescue calls a year and maintains 49 parks covering 1,072.03 acres. Police and fire cost $172.3 million to run, against proposed property taxes of $150.2 million.

If a buyer asks why a Boca Raton bill looks the way it does, the City's Property Taxes Explained brochure shows each authority's share of the $693,362,086 that residents pay each year. The School Board takes 37.18 percent and Palm Beach County operating and debt takes 26.74 percent.

The payment window runs from November through March, with delinquency beginning in April and no discount in March.

The Palm Beach County Tax Collector's early payment ladder gives 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January and 1 percent in February. Gross tax is due March 31, and a deadline that lands on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

After delinquency, the tax cannot be paid online, and a postmark no longer counts as proof. A payment has to arrive by the last working day of the month to count for that month. The delinquent line can confirm a balance.

sections.h2: Exemptions and caps for Boca Raton homes
sections.html:
Homestead applications go to the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser by March 1, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1.

A homestead exemption of $50,000 applies against most levies and $25,000 against school district tax, since the second $25,000 does not apply to school taxes. Amendment 1 created a double homestead exemption for all levies except school.

  • Save Our Homes holds yearly assessed value growth to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower. Florida's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026.
  • Portability can carry the benefit to a new homestead within three years.
  • A sale means a new owner is assessed at full just value the following January.
  • Seniors, disabled ex-servicemembers and deployed servicemembers have separate exemptions through state law and local ordinance.

Boca Raton has 101,582 residents in about 29 square miles of land. Owners live in 65.7 percent of homes, and the median home value is $722,700. Median gross rent is $2,508 and median household income is $106,273. Residents 65 and over are 24.6 percent of the population, so many sellers are retirees downsizing or heirs settling an estate. The city counts 49,050 dwelling units and an assessed value of $42.7 billion.

At these values, the tax adjustments at closing are large. Florida's deed stamp tax, 70 cents per $100 of price outside Miami-Dade, falls on every party to the deed, and the closing statement should divide the year's tax and any fire assessment.

sections.h2: If you fall behind on tax
sections.html:
Contact the Tax Collector before the April delinquency date. Delinquent tax cannot go through the online portal, and a payment mailed late is judged by its arrival date. Have the bill number from the Property Control Number box on your notice ready when you call. An installment plan and a homestead tax deferral are both available through the Tax Collector.

Deferral applications are due March 31 on Form DR-570, and installment applications by May 1 of the assessment year. Tax certificates are sold by June 1, a holder can seek a tax deed after two years, and on homestead property the opening deed bid includes half the assessed value.

A house with a certificate can still be sold, with payoff made from proceeds at closing. Ask the Tax Collector for a written payoff, since delinquent balances change as months pass.

A few steps in a sensible order help any Boca Raton sale go smoothly.

  1. Check your Property Appraiser record for the correct owner name, mailing address and exemptions.
  2. Ask the Tax Collector for the amount owed and whether the discount window is still open.
  3. Look at the bill for the fire assessment so you can explain it to buyers.
  4. Give the figures to your title company early so the closing statement shows the right split.

A cash sale skips the lender and appraisal. It does not skip the tax proration, the deed stamp tax or the payoff of any lien.

faqs.q: Does the City of Boca Raton send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city and seven other taxing authorities.

faqs.q: What is the Boca Raton millage rate?
faqs.a: It depends on the location. The city's sample prints 3.6639 mills for the city operating and debt levy and a total of 16.9090, labeled as the 2026-27 proposed figure. Check your parcel's final rate with the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: When do Boca Raton property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Gross tax is due March 31, and delinquent tax cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about a Boca Raton exemption?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, at (561) 355-2866. Applications are due on March 1.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A change of ownership resets assessed value to just value the following January 1, with limited exceptions such as certain spousal transfers.
